thread.title: Nasdaq futures climb, led higher by Apple’s jump - MarketWatch

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: Nasdaq futures climb, led higher by Apple’s jump - MarketWatch
text:
U.S. stocks mostly traded lower Wednesday afternoon, after initially edging slightly higher, as the Federal Reserve acknowledged rising prices and said it now expects inflation to “run near” its 2% target “over the medium term,” in its most recent policy statement. The central bank held key rates unchanged, as expected.
What are the main benchmarks doing? The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.12% was trading down 40 points, or 0.2%, at 24,055. The S&P 500 index SPX, -0.15% retreated by 6 points, or 0.2%, to 2,648, pressured by a sharp decline in consumer-staples stocks, down 1.8% on the day.
Meanwhile, the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +0.20% added 12 points to 7,144, an advance of 0.2%.
What’s driving markets? Fed officials wrapped up a two-day meeting, saying it expects further interest rate hikes will be needed in coming months. However, there was little in the statement that gave traders clarity over how many rate hikes are in the cards. The market is pricing in a high probability that the next interest-rate increase will come next month.
In total, fed-funds futures, used by investors to wager on short-term rates, indicate that Wall Street is pricing in roughly even-odds at the chance of three more rates hikes in 2018.
In corporate news, Apple ’s stock AAPL, +5.02% was helping buoy the tech sector, with the largest U.S. company by market value gaining 5%, after late Tuesday posting better-than-anticipated earnings and revenue for the first quarter.
Check out: Apple earnings were saved by the company’s new MVP
And see: The surprise in Apple earnings—big growth in China
The iPhone maker was merely the latest high-profile company to top analyst forecasts in its results. However, even better-than-expected earnings haven’t been enough to lift the main equity benchmarks out of a tight range in recent weeks , as investors are also worried about protectionism and other geopolitical flare-ups.
Which economic data are in focus? Don’t miss: Why the Fed could make 4 rate hikes this year
In the latest economic data, the private sector added 204,000 jobs in April , according to ADP. While this was above forecasts, it was also down from the 241,000 added in the previous month.
Check out: MarketWatch’s Economic Calendar
What are market analysts saying? “There are concerns in the market that rising inflation will prompt the Fed to hike more than three times this year, but the Fed statement was reassuring as it did not hint of faster pace of hikes,” said Kate Warne, investment strategist at Edward Jones.
“While this is positive for markets, we should be careful to assigns today’s modest moves to the Fed statement. Small moves often happen without any news,” Warne said.
Which stocks are moving? Snap Inc. SNAP, -21.55% plummeted 18% a day after reporting revenue and active daily users that were below forecasts .
Yum Brands Inc . YUM, -6.78% reported first-quarter earnings and sales that beat expectations . The fast-food chain operator also affirmed its full-year guidance. Shares fell 5.8%.
CVS Health Corp. CVS, -2.63% fell 3.2% despite reporting adjusted first-quarter earnings that beat expectations, along with better-than-expected sales .
Southern Co. SO, +0.31% reported first-quarter revenue that beat expectations, and earnings that were helped by the recently passed tax bill . The stock rose 0.6%.
Madison Square Garden Co . MSG, +1.30% swung to a first-quarter profit and reported revenue that topped analyst forecasts . The stock rose 1.5%.
Wyndham Worldwide Corp. WYN, -4.52% reported a sharp drop in its first-quarter earnings , although sales rose modestly. Shares fell 4%.
SodaStream International Ltd. SODA, -7.82% reported first-quarter earnings that beat expectations . It also raised its outlook. However, the stock lost 4.5%.
After the market closes, earnings releases should come from Kraft Heinz Co . KHC, -2.42% and Tesla Inc . TSLA, +1.81% among others.
Esperion Therapeutics Inc. ESPR, -31.05% announced results for a late-stage clinical trial of its cholesterol-lowering medication. The stock plummeted 26%.
What are other markets doing? European stocks SXXP, +0.63% rose modestly, supported by upbeat corporate results . U.K. stocks UKX, +0.30% added 0.4%.
Markets in Asia were little changed. Stocks in Japan NIK, -0.16% dipped 0.2%. Investors were awaiting cues from U.S.-China trade negotiations , along with the release of both a raft of April manufacturing data from Asia and the Federal Reserve’s latest policy statement.
Gold futures GCM8, +0.36% finished the session at a two-moth low but popped after the Fed statement, while U.S. oil futures settled higher . The ICE U.S. Dollar Index DXY, +0.02% fell 0.1% a day after turning positive for 2018.
—Victor Reklaitis contributed to this article
